basis: Venous occlusion by an embolized thrombus is a vascular disorder; it does not itself establish a blood-cell or coagulation disorder.
Acute epiglottitis is typically an infection of the upper airway.
Inflammation directly affects the duodenum; infectious or immune mechanisms are not intrinsic to every case.
Primary brain calcification affects the basal ganglia; the listed ocular finding occurs in only 1/13 patients.
The definition specifies carcinoma involving bone; heterogeneous child concepts do not establish other commonly affected organs.
Acantholytic blistering defines disease of oral and laryngeal mucosa; oral erosions and blisters are documented in 1/1 patients.
Marrow failure; brain defects 11/12 and developmental delay 2/2, cardiac defects 3/3, absent thumbs 3/4. Cap omits hearing, endocrine, ocular and renal abnormalities.
Hereditary noncirrhotic portal hypertension is a hepatic portal vascular disorder; cirrhosis and other downstream complications are not assumed.
Defective NK-cell cytotoxicity defines immunodeficiency; recurrent infections do not establish lasting damage to additional organs.
Anencephaly is a major brain malformation; adrenal hypoplasia is frequent (30-79%). Other listed structural defects occur in only 5-29%.
Thymic epithelial origin has no matching axis; this is not lymphoma. Lung/liver metastases are reported together in ~30%, without establishing either organ individually at >=30%.
Prostate epithelial carcinoma affects a reproductive organ outside the axes; familial occurrence does not establish additional organ damage.
Malignant neoplasm originates in the great vessels; pulmonary artery or vein origin remains cardiovascular.
DOK7-related fetal akinesia reflects neuromuscular-junction dysfunction with congenital contractures and limb deformities; subtype-specific pulmonary damage frequency is not established.
Isolated syndactyly is a congenital structural abnormality of the digits.
Congenital pseudarthrosis directly affects the fibula and its structural integrity.
Severe early obesity and global developmental impairment define the syndrome; hypotonia does not independently establish skeletal muscle disease.
Hypogonadotropism defines disease; olfactory loss is a major Kallmann diagnostic feature. Hearing impairment 3/14 and dental or bone abnormalities 2/14 are below 30%.
Developmental cataract affects the lens; the definition explicitly describes a nonsyndromic eye disorder.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder, also with adrenal insufficiency; developmental delay, dystonia and brain malformation occur in 1/1, as does structural hip dysplasia.
Wormian skull bones and brachydactyly define skeletal malformations; the definition distinguishes this from the allelic syndrome with congenital heart defects.
Mucocutaneous hamartomas and neurodevelopmental abnormalities characterize PHTS; GI polyps occur in >80% of evaluated patients. Cancer risks alone add no organs.
Hip dysplasia, premature epiphyseal fusion and cartilaginous bone lesions define the disease.
Encephalopathy, metabolic dysfunction and subcutaneous fat loss define disease; hepatic steatosis occurs in 30-79%. Myopathy and respiratory failure occur in only 5-29%.
Inflammatory colorectal polyps define disease; associated gastritis remains gastrointestinal. An autoimmune or infectious mechanism is not established by inflammation alone.
